full_judgment:
6. The limitation with respect to seeking election to Parliament, as contained in the proviso to clause (2) of Section 56 of the Order, shows the extent of the connection a teacher may have with any other lawful organisation. While a teacher may support the views or programme of any particular party inside Parliament, at present, it may be noted, there is only party, he is not allowed to seek election for becoming a member of Parliament, the reason, as it appears to us, is that if a teacher is allowed to seek election as a member of Parliament that will come into conflict with his professional duties as a whole-time teacher of the University. From the limitations with regard to seeking election to Parliament, as contained in the proviso, the legislative intention is clear that a teacher should not actively participate in an organisation, far less become one of its office bearers. It would be too narrow an interpretation, if the prohibition in the proviso is construed merely to apply to Parliament and not to any other organisation such as, a Union Parishad. The proviso does, not doubt, expressly apply to Parliament but taken in conjunction with the provisions in clause (2), the intention seems to be clear that a teacher or officer of the University has not been allowed the freedom to keep association with an organisation by becoming its office bearer. 

 Under these Rules any person who is elected a Chairman of the Union Parishad becomes entitled to receive certain pecuniary benefit, such benefit may not be in the form of a regular monthly salary but is nonetheless pecuniary when given in the form of an honorarium as mentioned in these Rules. The expressions "drive any pecuniary benefit from such association" do necessarily refer to a Chairman of an Union Parishad, thus making it quite obvious that in respect of the post of the Chairman the limitation must be extended, irrespective of the fact that the petitioner did not yet draw any honorarium.
